CITY OF ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
  COMMISSION
  THURSDAY, JANUARY 8, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Environmental Sustainability Commission will be held on Thursday, January
8, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in Conference Room A, on the second floor of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First St., Alhambra, California, pursuant to the
order of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission Secretary.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Latoya Waters,
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability
  Commission Secretary

Notice No. N2M25-187
Posted: 01/05/2026
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  January 8, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Katie Chan, Scott Chan, Jeffery Gomez, Xana Hermosillo, Michael Scaduto

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve 11-13-2025 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit
  all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior to the
  meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, March 12, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.

  If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
  the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
  make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

  If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
  heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
  which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard
  under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the

01/05/2026
 Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:02 p.m. on November 13, 2025.

I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Katie Chan, Xana Hermosillo, Michael Scaduto

  Staff Present: Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities serving as Commission
  Secretary

  Members of the Public:
  Alexandra Lopez – Active SGV
  Marlene Buenrostro – Active SGV

II. VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES
  The Commission reviewed and approved the minutes from the previous meeting
  on May 8, 2025.

  Commissioner Hermosillo motioned to approve the meeting minutes from May 8,
  2025. Commissioner Scaduto seconded the motion. As three (3) were in
  attendance and two (2) motioned and seconded, respectively, the motion passed.

III. SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE

  Staff did not provide an update as there is backend work being completed to prepare
  to possibly go before Council in January 2026. It is anticipated that the
  Sustainability Plan will be presented before the Commission before going to
  Council.

IV. SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION
  No action items to discuss.

  Commissioner Hermosillo raised a question: Is it possible for the Commission to
  be more involved with projects and groundbreaking ceremonies?
  L. Waters responded: Yes, it is possible. It is my understanding that the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission was developed under the purpose to
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

  assist with the Sustainability Plan. Environmental is such a large scope – water,
  stormwater, solid waste, groundbreaking with various related projects.
  Commissioner Scaduto: Where are we with the Sustainability Plan? Is it already a
  draft and are they working to finalize it?
  L. Waters: Yes, the Plan is still in draft. Staff are working to incorporate comments
  received from the community meetings.
  Commissioner Scaduto: Is the draft available online?
  L. Waters: I am not sure if the draft is available online. I will double check and
  circle back to you all.
  Commissioner Scaduto: What happens after the Plan update? How can we play a
  bigger role in the community? We would like to find an identity to focus on. Is
  there anything in the City we can focus on within the City that the Commission can
  work on?
  L. Waters: On the Water Quality side of Environmental we have a few large-scale
  projects underway, Story Park Project, Burke Heritage and Marengo Yard
  Stormwater Project, and the Green Street Demonstration Project on Main Street.
  These projects are in three (3) different phases. Green Streets Project: the City is
  looking to secure a Construction Manager with Council approval at the next
  meeting in December. An outreach meeting was held for Burke Heritage Park
  (apologies for the late notification to you all) as we approach 90% design. Finally,
  Story Park project is also underway. There will be additional outreach opportunities
  where the Commissioners can be involved. Staff are working to integrate all aspects
  of Environmental, including Water Quality into the Sustainability Plan. We will
  circle back to look for opportunities where the Commissioners can play a bigger
  role.

V. BURKE HERITAGE PARK AND MARENGO TREATMENT PLANT
  PROJECT OUTREACH
  Active San Gabriel Valley (Active SGV) presented project educational outreach
  efforts and information to the commission. Active SGV began by providing a
  project overview. Highlighting the project purpose is to enhance community
  aesthetics and functionality by reducing stormwater runoff and pollutants through
  sustainable infrastructure, while adding recreational features.

  Question: Commissioner Hermosillo – How much does this project reduce the open
  space that is currently used for things like soccer?
  L. Waters – I do not have an exact percentage, but this concern was discussed at
  our last community outreach meeting. The space will still provide room for pick-
  up soccer games and open space for the community. Organized sports are
  prohibited in the park.

  Page 2 of 7
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

Question: Commissioner Scaduto – Is there any consideration to incorporate
(public) restrooms at the park?
L. Waters – restrooms were not considered as this park is considered a (passing)
leisure space where visitors typically enjoy short, casual strolls rather than
extended stays. For this reason, the project will not fully illuminate the park space
but rather incorporate security lighting as there is a water feature onsite.
The stormwater capture and water quality improvements include the following:
  •  Dry well
  •  Seasonal bioswale (wetland)
  •  Biofiltration areas
The total anticipated retention is 46,000 gallons of stormwater. Providing
stormwater treatment for a 111-acre area of Alhambra and South Pasadena.
The community benefits include the following:
  •  Enhanced Park space – nature-based amenities.
  •  Expanded tree canopy – new trees and native plants.
  •  Reduced heat island effect – greenery, water management and bioretention
  creating cooler spaces.
  •  Improved stormwater management – reduce localize flooding and
  pollutants to waterways.
  •  Community friendly amenities – picnic areas, seating nooks, and pedestrian
  paths.
Construction is anticipated to begin at the end of June 2026 and continue through
April/May 2027. Partial street closures are expected and will be announced in
advance. The project is funded through the Safe, Clean Water Program
administered by the Los Angeles County Flood Control District, Statewide Park
Program, the California Native Plant Demonstration and Educational Grant, and
the City of Alhambra.
Question: Commissioner Scaduto – Is the Safe, Clean Water Program
infrastructure funding?
L. Waters – Yes.
Question: Commissioner Scaduto – Is the cost still within the budget? Will you be
asking for more money within the program?
L. Waters – We anticipate the project cost will remain within budget, With the
Green Streets project the Engineer’s Estimate was $8.4 Million, the lowest bidder
was $6.3 Million. If we continue with that trend, our Engineer’s Estimate for the
Burk Heritage Project is $4.4 Million we will stay within budget. Should the

  Page 3 of 7
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

project need additional funding we will look at the municipal return funds or
request additional funding from the Safe, Clean Water Program.
Question: Commissioner Scaduto – What about O&M? Will the City ask for
additional funds?
L. Waters – Our City staff will be responsible for O&M.
Question: Commissioner K. Chan – Is there existing lighting infrastructure?
L. Waters – Yes, there is existing lighting infrastructure. It does not illuminate the
entire park. The Historical Museum does have perimeter lighting.
Question: Commissioner Hermosillo – Both Alhambra Rd and Bushnell will be
closed during construction?
L. Waters – Yes, likely not simultaneously. We will avoid creating unnecessary
traffic congestion and reduce adverse impact to the community, including Iona
Workspace.
Active SGV Staff proceeded with additional questions directed to the
Commissioners:
  •  What do you like most about Burke Heritage Park today and what works
  well?
  o Commissioner Hermosillo – I like all the trees and the shade
  currently available. It is an underutilized park.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – I echo those comments. It is an
  underutilized space. It is a good stopping place on the way to
  Alhambra Park. It does lack seating. Will there be additional seating
  to enjoy the area?
  o Commissioner K. Chan – A good green space.
  •  What are some current challenges at Burke Heritage Park?
  o Commissioner Hermosillo – People doing sport activities in the
  park take up a good portion of the open space. How would we share
  this space? There are a lot of people who take their dogs off the
  leash at this park, although there is signage prohibiting such.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – Lack of restrooms. I understand the trade-
  offs.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – Would like to see the park more utilized.
  •  What opportunities will emerge from Burke Heritage Park and Marengo
  Yard Project being implemented?
  o Commissioner Hermosillo – The stormwater capture is great.
  People who read signs would like to know why there was a change
  in the park.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – The back corner is underutilized. The
  project will encourage people to take a nature walk back there.

  Page 4 of 7
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

  o Commissioner K. Chan – Signage and education will be a nice
  addition to the project.
•  What concerns do you have about the project?
  o Commissioner Scaduto – Has the project been altered based on
  feedback?
   Active SGV - Yes. The community is split between enjoying
  the current conditions of the park and wanting to see the
  proposed changes to the park.
  o Commissioner Scaduto - What’s the biggest negative feedback
  received?
   Active SGV - The walkability was a concern to make the
  area safter to access.
   L. Waters – We are looking at enhancing the pedestrian
  crossings for safety, such as installing flashing beacons.
  Possible considerations for an additional crosswalk.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – The uniqueness of the project can be a
  concern as stormwater capture is a rather new concept.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – Is this the first stormwater capture project?
   L. Waters – No, the City has a stormwater capture project in
  the Stoneman Parking Lot, just behind “Ross”. There is a
  large, perforated pipe designed to capture stormwater and
  recharge groundwater sources. Green Streets Project will
  begin construction before the Burke Heritage Park Project.
  The projects may be under construction simultaneously, but
  neither will deflect or reflect the other.
•  Do you support the Burke Heritage Park and Marengo Yard Stormwater
  Capture Project?
  o Commissioner Hermosillo – Yes.
  o Commissioner Scaduto – Yes. What is the nexus between the
  Marengo Yard the Burke Heritage side of the project?
   L. Waters – Initially we were going to infiltrate at the
  Marengo Yard, but it is not feasible to disrupt the
  infrastructure at the Yard. We will divert stormwater to
  prevent flooding and slow down onsite flows with rock beds.
  Reduce stormwater runoff from spool piles by protecting
  these piles and eliminate potential for discharge.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – Yes, I support the project.
•  What do you look forward to most once the stormwater and park
  enhancements are implemented?
  o Commissioner Scaduto – The opportunity to use this as a
  demonstration project.

  Page 5 of 7
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

  o Commissioner Hermosillo – The educational component. This is a
  good space to show different things happening in one place.
  Bioretention and native plants.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – Excited to see the new plantings and trees
  how this will integrate into the system.
  o Commissioner K. Chan – When will the community outreach
  period end? How will the community submit feedback?
   Active SGV – contact the City (Latoya Waters –
  lwaters@alhambraca.gov) directly.
   L. Waters – The outreach is ongoing throughout the project.
  Additional feedback will not be included unless it comes up
  during CEQA or is imperative to community safety.
  o Commissioner Scaduto - Is there anything you need assistance with?
  Can we offer support?
   L. Waters. Not currently for this project. Is it a great idea to
  incorporate the Commission into project outreach and
  support.

VI. PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

VII. COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Commissioner Scaduto – Curious to know what is the new iteration of the projects
  that the Commissioners can feed into. Are there other street improvements options
  other than on the right-of-way?
  L. Waters – The City does require low impact development considerations for
  private projects throughout the City. We are looking for opportunities to
  incorporate low impact development in our street projects. Staff are working to
  understand how to incorporate such considerations in Public Works, Utilities, and
  Parks.
  Commissioner Hermosillo – Active transportation considerations can be
  incorporated. Is there a way for the Environmental Sustainability Commission to
  be involved with approvals of some sort, like the Art Commission? Inclusion in
  projects? It would be great for us to advocate for projects, green construction,
  native planting.
  Commissioner Scaduto – Has school districts and sites been considered in
  Alhambra?
  L. Waters – A few years back, it is my understanding that the City initiated project
  discussions with the district. We would like to consider more opportunities to
  include Alhambra schools.

  Page 6 of 7
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on November 13, 2025

  Commissioner Scaduto – I would like to share expertise to overcome hurdles with
  school districts.
  Commissioner Hermosillo – There are not many trees around Alhambra High, and
  it is rather hot walking the school perimeter.
  Commissioner K. Chan – I would like to see Alhambra School district included
  with more projects in the City.

VIII. ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner K. Chan adjourned the meeting at 6:43 p.m.

  Page 7 of 7

ITEM # II

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on January 8, 2026

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:04 p.m. on January 8, 2026.

I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Commissioner S. Chan, Commissioner Gomez,
  Commissioner Hermosillo, Commissioner Scaduto

  Staff Present: Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities serving as Commission
  Secretary

  Members of the Public:
  None Present

II. VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES
  The Commission reviewed and approved the minutes from the previous meeting
  on November 13, 2025.

  Commissioner Scaduto motioned to approve the minutes and Commissioner
  Gomez second. Motion passed.

III. SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  L. Waters read into record an email from the City’s Sustainability Analyst:

  “The complete draft of the comprehensive Environmental Sustainability Plan will
  be presented to the City Council on Monday, February 23, 2026. This will kick-off
  a month-long public comment opportunity during which residents, business,
  communities, organizations, and other stakeholders can review the plan and
  provide comments. The plan will be posted on the City’s website along with
  instructions to submit comments. The City will host virtual and in-person
  community meetings and conduct outreach at local events: Farmer’s Market, Lunar
  New Year Festival, and possibly our Eco Fair to promote the plan and encourage
  residents to review the final draft. We will send notifications about the public
  meeting events once plans are finalized. Commissioners are encouraged to attend
  these meetings and events. We will also have more information at the March
  Environmental Sustainability Commission Meeting.”

  Commissioner Gomez: When are the public meetings?
  L. Waters: They have not been scheduled yet. I will provide notification once I
  receive additional information about the meetings. The kick-off will be initiated
  by the Council Meeting where the Sustainability Team will present and with
  Council’s approval the [public] meetings will be scheduled.
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on January 8, 2026

Commissioner Scaduto: Is it a month-long comment period?
L. Waters: As of right now, yes that is anticipated.

Commissioner Scaduto: Will we be provided an advance copy to provide
comments?
L. Waters: I will make a note to send over the Plan to you all once Council approves
the Draft Plan.

Commissioner Hermosillo: Should we watch the Council Meeting or will the
presentation be repeated to us?
L. Waters: You all can attend and tune-in but the information will also be presented
to you all.

Commissioner Gomez: Who will be here if we have questions on the plan?
L. Waters: The Sustainability Analyst, Katie Martel and the Consultant will attend
to answer any questions. I believe our Assistant City Manager will also be in
attendance.

Commissioner S. Chan: Are there any outreach events scheduled before our next
meeting?
L. Waters: Yes. The Lunar Festival is scheduled in February.

Commissioner S. Chan: Can we make sure the outreach documents are translated
for the Vietnamese and Chinese Communities?
L. Waters: [making note]

Commissioner Scaduto: Is there a push on social media?
L. Waters: Our newly hired Public Information Specialist will be responsible for
social media updates.

Commissioner Gomez: What does the public outreach at the Lunar New Year
[Festival] look like? Will there be a booth?
L. Waters: Yes, there will be a booth. In past practice there has been poster boards,
surveys, handouts, and sign-in sheets to obtain additional project information.

Commissioner Hermosillo: Saturday February 28 is the Lunar New Year Festival.

Commissioner Scaduto: Would it help the momentum if someone from this
Commission is there to support?
L. Waters: Would you all like to have a role in public outreach at the Lunar
Festival?

Commissioners unanimously in agreement and want to be involved with Lunar
New Year Outreach.

Commissioner Gomez: How comprehensive is the Plan?
L. Waters: It is comprehensive, staff received a briefing of the modules (if you
will) within the Plan that would be subject to our departments and divisions,
respectively. My Department, we covered the water aspect, waste management,

  Page 2 of 4
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on January 8, 2026

  mobility-bicycle lanes (as we are part of Public Works), green space, creating green
  opportunities, and projects. There is a list of action items that will be updated in
  the plan, depending on comments received from other Departments. Stormwater
  aspects will also be included along with trash and compliance with the Trash
  TMDL. It’s intended to capture everything we have been working on in our
  individual departments. The Plan is a “living document” and will be updated along
  the way.

  Commissioner Scaduto: Is this a Plan the other Commissions and Commissioners
  are being asked to review as well, being there is a lot of overlap?
  L. Waters: Not to my knowledge. I would assume the Transportation Commission
  will see the Plan as there is a mobility aspect. However, I am not sure if it has been
  brought before the Transportation Commission.

  Commissioner S. Chan: As some of the Sustainability Plans have such high-level
  language, can it be brought down to a sixth-grade level [for general community
  understanding]?
  L. Waters: [making note]

  Commissioner Hermosillo: If we can ensure in-person meetings are held across
  the City? and ensure at least 2-weeks’ notice?
  L. Waters: [making note]

  Commissioner Scaduto: Will there be an email blast using information from sign
  in sheets?
  L. Waters: It can be. However, at the time the information was obtained it was for
  project specific information to be distributed. We will have the information on our
  website, newsletter, as well as social media.

  Commissioner S. Chan: If we know of large groups that would like a presentation.
  Does the City have the capacity?
  L. Waters: We have to make sure all meetings are accessible to the general public
  and everyone has the same opportunity to attend.

IV. ENVIRONMENTL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN DISCUSSION

  Discussed in the aforementioned section.

V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  No public attendees present.

VI. COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Commissioner Scaduto: How can we [Commissioners] get more involved. Still
  thinking about what is going on from an infrastructure stance throughout the City
  outside of the Sustainability Plan.

  L. Waters: There are quite a few plans underway. We are updating our Water Master
  Plan and our Sewer Master Plan, allowing us to assess our sewer and water
  infrastructure and ensure we are in compliance. If there is interest in our other

  Page 3 of 4
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting on January 8, 2026

  projects, we can arrange for these projects to be presented before the Commission.

  Commissioner Gomez: Is there any way we can talk to people in the City to be
  more hands on? To have more interface and interaction with the people involved?
  L. Waters: That is the idea of having presentations [at the Commission meetings],
  to obtain first-hand knowledge from the project team.

  Commissioner Hermosillo: I met with Councilman Maza and expressed interest in
  how we can be apart (in small part at least) of the Community Center. It seems like
  there are many opportunities for Sustainability to be involved.
  L. Waters: That is the whole premise behind the Plan to get everyone to the table
  with one central plan. This will help us push forward our projects and future
  endeavors in the City.

VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Commissioner Hermosillo adjourned the meeting at 6:26 p.m.
